##### Project general facts

The Row Saadiyat by Aldar is a boutique village of seven sculptural residential buildings conceived by Bjarke Ingels Group, with fluid, organic lines that harmonise with natural light and landscape. Each building rises from a ground floor to nine residential levels, with light facades, panoramic windows and horizontal balconies, while layered lighting creates a sculptural effect in the evening. The collection includes one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments, with selected layouts offering a study or a maid's room.

Residents enjoy a curated lifestyle of boutique cafes, fine dining and wellness clubs, together with co-working lounges and a private members' club, all connected by shaded, climate-controlled walkways that encourage exploration in every season. Boutique retail stores, a gourmet supermarket, a luxury spa, curated kids' clubs, boutique fitness studios, a wellness pod and pet spa and grooming services complete an offer that balances the energy of city life with the tranquillity of home.

Interiors by Kettle Collective merge artistry and practicality, combining soothing natural textures, warm tones, thoughtful functionality and soft diffused lighting. Smooth timber floors and sun-washed cabinetry form a calm backdrop, while bedrooms offer quiet, comfortable retreats. Kitchens combine intelligent storage, premium built-in appliances and sleek finishes to make daily life both functional and beautiful. Homes are delivered with fitted kitchens and appliances, leaving furniture to the owner's own taste and style.

##### Location description and benefits

Saadiyat Island is Abu Dhabi's cultural heart, blending world-class museums and institutions with pristine beaches and a tranquil lifestyle. The Saadiyat Cultural District is home to Louvre Abu Dhabi, Zayed National Museum, Guggenheim Abu Dhabi and the Abrahamic Family House, alongside luxury hotels, beach resorts, fine dining venues and leading educational institutions, creating a calm and inspiring setting for everyday life.

Zayed National Museum and Louvre Abu Dhabi are a short drive away, as are Saadiyat Beach, Mamsha Al Saadiyat, NYU Abu Dhabi and the Saadiyat Beach Golf Club. Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Highway connects the island with Al Reem Island, Al Maryah Island, the city centre, Yas Island and Zayed International Airport, all within easy reach, keeping the wider capital comfortably close.

Saadiyat Island is an investment zone open to international buyers and one of the most prestigious addresses in the UAE. Architect-designed residences within a walkable village close to the cultural district are in limited supply, supporting strong demand from high-net-worth buyers and premium tenants. The island's cultural offer, beaches and connectivity underpin long-term value and resilient resale prospects for owners and investors.
